questions.q: What is the author's central argument?
options: Nonprofits are obsolete now that AI wealth has been created
Mission-driven companies may be key institutions alongside philanthropy
Philanthropy should be abandoned in favor of pure investing
AI fortunes will never be given away by this generation
questions.explain: He argues the strongest mission-driven firms make social good the unit economics, beyond the 'two ledgers' model.

questions.q: What did Carnegie's 'Gospel of Wealth' argue?
options: Wealth should be passed to heirs to build family dynasties
Direct charity to the poor is the best form of giving
Companies should avoid giving until after the founder dies
The rich should give strategically in life through enduring institutions
questions.explain: It said 'the man who dies rich dies disgraced' and favored institutions over charity.

questions.q: Who did Rockefeller hire as essentially the first professional philanthropic strategist?
options: Bill Gates
John Gates
Nan Ransohoff
Frederick Gates
questions.explain: He hired Frederick Gates, no relation to Bill.

questions.q: What is the size and goal of Stripe's Intercept Fund?
options: $500m to eradicate respiratory infections
$500m to build libraries in rural American towns
$50m to speed up climate research and carbon removal
$1b to fund open AI safety research at universities
questions.explain: Stripe announced a $500m initiative to eradicate respiratory infections.

questions.q: What does the author imply about the check as a vehicle for good?
options: It should be taxed more heavily to fund public goods
It is not the only way; companies aligned with outcomes count
It is unnecessary now that companies can solve everything
It is the best way, so companies should not try to help
questions.explain: He says the check is not the only vehicle and company incentives aligned with outcomes should count too.
